APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JULY 19, 2022

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:03 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Alma D. Puente, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Pro Tem Puente
  s) Councilmember Herrera  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:04 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:01 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8 – Conference with
  Real Property Negotiator:

  Property Location:
  8575-017-909, 8575-019-907, 8575-019-908, 8575-019-910, 8575-019-911,
  8575-019-912, 8575-019-913, 8575-021-932, 8575-021-934, 8575-021-936

  Name of Party City is Negotiation with:
  UTH Holding I, LLC
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 19, 2022

  City’s Representative in the Negotiations:
  Alma K. Martinez, City Manager; Betty Donavanik, Community & Economic
  Development Director; and Lloyd Pilchen, Assistant City Attorney

  Under Discussion:
  Discussion of price and terms.

  Update was provided, feedback given, but no final action taken.

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a), 54956.9(d)(2)
  and 54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Facts and
  Circumstances which May Create Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Update was provided, feedback given, but no final action taken.

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association; and All
  Unrepresented Employees of City Executive Team.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma K. Martinez, City Manager and John Nguyen,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  Update was provided, feedback given, but no final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  City Council. George Ussery, Evangelical Methodist

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Mayor Ancona

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: None

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 19, 2022

  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Alisha Lopez – Day One wanted to thank the City Council, City Manager and Parks &
  Recreation with working hand in hand to make the Getty 25 event possible.

  Lu P. Cruz – Spoke about the City Attorney’s Office being overpaid.

  Julio Ramirez – Provided a pamphlet regarding street vendors and spoke about the
  pamphlet. Also mentioned that bathrooms at parks are closed.

  Irma Zamorano – Thank the Mayor, spoke about he officers. Spoke about the City
  Attorney’s Office payments.

  Rodolfo – Spoke about the City Attorney’s Office payments.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Spoke about the City Attorney’s Office payments. Spoke about the
  street vendors.

  Written Comment:

  Christy Zamani – would like to thank the City Council, City Manager, and El Monte Parks
  and Recreation Department for working hand in hand with us to make the Getty 25 Event
  possible

  Alex De Vries – Writing to express my sincere gratitude for all the hard work that was put
  into sponsoring and promoting the Getty 25 Festival that occurred this past weekend

  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke the current 3-2 votes; approval of district elections; the Assistant
  City Managers. Mentioned the January 6th Committee meetings in Washington.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: None

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-668

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS

  1106832 through 1107493, and the payroll period June 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

  16.1  Discussion Regarding Memorial Committee.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Discussion on Shein Art Campaign Program with Commissioning of Murals
  on Main Street and Other City Locations.

  Shein has reached out showing interest in commissioning six (6) murals in
  total to the City. The Council is in agreement with having more art within the
  City. Would like for City staff to reach out to Shein.

  18A.2 Update and Discussion on Memorializing Sergeant Michael Paredes and
  Officer Joseph Santana.

  There will be a committee that will be put in place to memorialize our officers.

  18A.3 Update and Discussion on Community Clean-Up Events.

  It is my understanding that there were quarterly cleaning events. It would be
  great to establish quarterly cleaning events throughout the City focusing on
  areas of need. May want to get organizations who want to volunteer.

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 19, 2022

  18A.4 Update and Discussion on El Monte Police Department Aero Bureau
  Program.

  The City Council has been in discussion with Officer Ron Danison regarding
  the need to start considering replacement of the helicopters. Would like to
  request an update regarding this matter.

  City Manager Martinez provided an update regarding this item and the
  budget gap that the City has to be able to address this item.

  Request for a presentation from staff to address the funding gap.

  Chief Lowry provided an update on the total cost of the helicopter and the
  funds that may be used.

  18A.5 Update and Discussion on Implementing Town Hall Meetings Regarding
  Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness.

  This is along the same lines of neighborhood watch and the STOP Program.
  Request to have town hall meetings regarding public safety, including the
  STOP Program and L.A. County Fire to talk about emergency preparedness
  in case of a natural disaster.

  Chief Lowry proposed that the City do a Public Safety Open House on a
  Saturday and get Fire to come out there in order to generate more of a
  response from the community.

  18A.6 Discussion and Update on Memorial Mural Honoring Sergeant Michael
  Paredes and Officer Joseph Santana.

  18A.7 Update and Discussion on Neighborhood Watch and Stop Program.

  I am glad that we are reaching out to the community.

  18A.8 Update on Human Relations Ad Hoc Committee.

  If staff can set up this meeting on July 21st.

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Puente

  18B.1 Discussion and Action Regarding District Election Public Outreach Plan.

  As the election season approaches it is important the community is informed
  as to the fact that Councilmembers will not be running based on districts.
  Has additional information been provided since this item was approved by
  the City Council.

  City Manager Martinez provided an update regarding work being done by the
  City’s PIO Elevate in regards to this item.

  18B.2 Discussion Regarding Guaranteed Income Pilot Program.

  Would like to know where the City is on Guaranteed Income Pilot Program
  and how close the City is to getting these benefits out to the community.

  City Manager Martinez provided an update regarding this program and where
  the City is at in regards to this.

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 19, 2022

18C.  Councilman Herrera

  Spoke about the national attention on the shootings taking place, is the City
  reassessing what it is doing to work with the school districts to improve
  safety at the schools.

  Chief Lowry provided an update regarding current conversations with
  Superintendent Zuniga.
  Mayor Ancona requested that the Police Department keep the lines of
  communication open. Spoke about the need of Resource Officers.

  18C.1 Update and Discussion Regarding Pavement Management Plan.

  Requested an update on the Pavement Management Plan.

  City Manager provided an update regarding the Pavement Management Plan.
  A report should be ready for review by the City Council closer to the end of
  the year.

  18C.2 Update and Discussion Regarding Tree Master Plan/Grid Pruning.

  Requested an update on the Tree Master Plan.

  The City Manager provided a quick update regarding work being done by the
  City’s contractor NorthStar.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Spoke about the Getty 25 Event. Thanked everyone who made this event a
  success.

  18D.1 Update and Discussion on Economic Development in the Flair Park Area.

  There have been developers who have been coming to Council asking for
  support and staff has been working with them. Feel like a vision should be
  created for that space. Asked City Manager to provide update regarding the
  Flair Park Area.

  City Manager Martinez provided an update regarding the Flair Park Area
  mentioned that there is a study that is in the works for the uses for the Flair
  Park Area.

  Request was made to bring back to the City Council with regards to the Flair
  Park Area as soon as possible.

  18D.2 Update Requested on the Administration Response to the Annual
  Comprehensive Financial Report.

  Would like to see where the City is at with the response to the Annual
  Comprehensive Financial Report.

  City Manager Martinez provided update on the process for the response to
  the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.

18E.  Councilwoman Dr. Morales

  18E.1 Discussion and Action Regarding the Development of a Strike Team to
  Provide Coordinated Enforcement of State and Municipal Laws Related to
  Motels and Hotels in the City.

  Spoke about the tragic event that took place on Garvey. Would like to
  develop a strike team that will include the Police Department and Code
  Enforcement.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 19, 2022

Chief Lowry will work with Code Enforcement to correct this.

Councilmember Martinez Muela - Years ago something similar was done to
enforce the codes that needed to be addressed.

Mayor Ancona spoke to the City Manager recently regarding the Garvey
Corridor.

18E.2 Discussion and Action Regarding a Ballot Initiative to Increase the
  Transient Occupancy Tax in the City of El Monte.

This is related to the issues with the Hotels and Motels. What is the process
on getting a ballot initiative on the November 8th ballot.
City Manager provided information on the last day to submit a resolution to
the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors to include this on the
November 8th ballot.

Councilmember Martinez Muela would like a presentation from staff on this
matter.

Staff to bring back a presentation on this item at the next meeting.

18E.3 Update and Discussion Regarding Critical Care Response Team (CCRT).

This will be brought back to the City Council next month. The City did
receive one response to address this mater.

18E.4 Update and Discussion Regarding Pioneer Park.

Curious to see where the City is at with regards to Pioneer Park.

City Manager provided an update. The City issued RFPs for this item.

The State is not providing the City with additional funding for this Park. The
City is in the process of negotiations with the State.

Councilmember Martinez Muela spoke about the bid challenges that the City
is facing with respect to this item.

18E.5 Update and Discussion Regarding Strategic Traffic Offender Program
  (STOP).

Chief Lowry provided an update regarding the STOP program and future
meetings.

18E.6 Update and Discussion on the Art House Repairs.

City Manager provided an update with regards to the Art House Repairs. The
contractor working on this found additional issues and the project has been
delayed a little but will be available next month.
